title: RingCentral call forwarding: How it works + limitations
summary: Get a complete guide to RingCentral call forwarding: how it works, setup steps, and its limitations versus modern VoIP platforms.
body_text: Imagine you’re finally clocking out for a well-deserved weekend. You’re driving home, music blasting, thinking about sinking into the couch with a bowl of popcorn. But your business number starts to ring. With a sigh, you answer. You’re surprised to learn it’s a simple customer support question that your on-call teammate should’ve answered. It’s time to choose a phone system that offers better call forwarding features. If you’re considering going with RingCentral for your call forwarding needs, you should understand what it can and can’t do. To access it, your admin has to activate call handling permissions for specific users. You can choose to forward all calls, create scheduling rules, or send callers to voicemail. You can also play a custom audio message if you prefer. The downside? There’s no visual editor for call forwarding. That means you’ll have to manually adjust your settings without seeing your call flows in context. This guide explores the key features and limitations of RingCentral call forwarding. You’ll learn about the different options available, how to set it up, and a RingCentral alternative that offers modern call forwarding for teams. How to forward calls on RingCentral RingCentral offers call handling and forwarding settings at two levels: for admins and for users. Admin-level forwarding lets account administrators set up call forwarding rules for other users. For example, you can set up business hours that affect incoming calls to the main company number. User-level forwarding is when reps add rules to their own number or user extension. They can adjust when calls come in during specific days and times. Here’s what these look like in greater detail. How to forward RingCentral calls as an admin As a RingCentral admin, you can manage call forwarding at the account level. This means you can make changes to your own phone number, as well as your entire team. There are two different types of calls you can forward: company calls and queue calls. Company calls refer to any incoming call that reaches your main business number. Creating forwarding rules will affect every inbound call to that number. For example, you could send all incoming after-hours calls to a voicemail inbox or an emergency backup number. Queue calls are groups of callers routed to specific groups. This could be an internal extension or a shared support number where multiple team members work together to answer calls. Forwarding rules for queue calls only affect calls coming to that specific group. For example, you can send all missed callers on your shared support number to RingCentral’s AI receptionist. Here’s how to set up call forwarding as an admin in RingCentral: Forward all company calls Sign in to the RingCentral Admin Portal . Click Phone System . Select the company number you wish to configure. Click Call Handling & Forwarding . If your business has multiple locations, click the site you want to manage, then click the Company Call Handling tab. Toggle on Forward All Company Calls . Select your forwarding destination. You can see a full list of these options in the Forward all company calls forwarding options section below. If you want to limit call forwarding to a specific window, check Specify start and end dates . Then enter the dates and times you want your call forwarding process to continue. Click Save to confirm your selections. Keep in mind you can also use the Admin Portal to configure business hours and your IVR menu, as well as schedule settings for after-hours calls. Forward all queue calls Sign in to the Admin Portal . Go to Phone System, Groups, and Call Queues . Click the call queue you want to modify. Click the Call Handling & Members dropdown. Click the Forward all queue calls toggle to turn it on. How to forward RingCentral calls as a user Individual users can set up their own call forwarding in RingCentral without admin access. There are two ways to do this: Forwarding all incoming calls to a specific destination Setting up call forwarding rules for during and after your business hours Note: This feature is available only if your Admin has provided you with call handling permissions. Here’s how to forward RingCentral calls as a user via the desktop, browser, and mobile apps: Desktop and web app To turn on Forward All Calls: Click your profile picture at the top left. Click Incoming call rules . Click the Forward all calls toggle to turn it on. Click Add schedule , then use the date and time selectors to set your call forwarding schedule. Select your forwarding destination. Click Save . Keep in mind that Forward All Calls will override any existing call handling settings for work hours. If you want to route calls differently after hours, you’ll need to set up standard call forwarding settings. To configure standard call forwarding settings: In the navigation bar, click Settings . Click Phone in the left panel. Click Incoming call rules . By default, incoming call rules apply 24/7. To set up a schedule for work and after-hours, click the Pencil icon to set a custom work schedule. To create a custom rule with a different schedule and call handling instructions, click Add Rule . Click the Welcome greeting toggles to turn on one or more options for callers. This could be a screening prompt, a notice of connection, or playing music. Under Ring settings , you can review and manage how your apps and devices will ring. Incoming calls will either: Ring in order: Devices ring one at a time Ring all at once: All numbers and devices ring simultaneously Toggle individual devices or numbers on or off to include or exclude them from the ring order. Click Add number or coworker if you want incoming calls to ring additional numbers or extensions. In the If no one answers section, click the dropdown to select how missed calls should be routed. We explain your options later in the guide. Click Save to confirm your settings. Mobile app To turn on Forward All Calls: Open the RingCentral mobile app. Tap your profile icon or navigate to Settings . Select Phone, then tap Incoming call rules . Toggle on Forward All Calls . Choose your forwarding destination. Tap Save to confirm. To configure standard call forwarding settings: Go to Settings , then tap Phone . Tap Incoming call rules . To set a custom work schedule and configure separate after-hours rules, click the Pencil icon . To create a custom rule with a different schedule or instructions, click Add Rule . Click the Welcome greeting toggles to turn on one or more options for callers. This could be a screening prompt, a notice of connection, or playing music. Set your preferred ring order. This could be ringing in order , or ringing all together . Toggle devices and numbers on or off to include them in your ring sequence. Set your preference for missed calls. For example, you might forward the call to an external number, send to voicemail, or play an announcement. Tap Save to save your changes. RingCentral call forwarding options There are multiple ways to forward your calls on every RingCentral pricing plan. These options can vary depending on the type of call forwarding you choose. This includes: Forward all calls forwarding options The Forward all calls feature in RingCentral lets you forward every incoming call to another destination when you can’t pick up the phone. This is configurable at the user level. That means you don’t need to be an admin to set this up for your RingCentral number. You can choose to forward all calls to: A voicemail inbox. You can also configure a custom greeting. Any extension or phone number. This includes numbers outside of RingCentral. A custom or general announcement. Play a recorded message, then end the call. Forward all company calls forwarding options If you’re a RingCentral admin, you can forward all incoming calls to your company’s main numbers. This can be useful during business closures, holidays, or emergencies. You can forward all company calls in RingCentral to the following destinations: A recorded announcement . Send calls to an extension that plays a recorded message and then disconnects. Voicemail . Send callers to a dedicated voicemail inbox so you can follow up later. A specific user . Send calls to a selected user or extension. Multiple users in a call queue . Send callers to a queue where multiple team members share responsibility for incoming calls. Company greeting . Play a default or custom greeting. AI Receptionist . RingCentral’s AI Receptionist, or AIR, can answer questions, screen leads, and forward calls to other team members. IVR menu . Send callers to a phone menu. Shared line . Send calls to a shared number, like for sales or customer support. Limited extension . Send calls to an extension with limited features that isn’t tied to a specific user. It may be useful when configuring RingCentral call recording , since you won’t have to tie the feature to an individual user’s account. Forward all queue calls forwarding options Forwarding all call queues will send every member of a queue to a separate destination. That way, they can bypass the queue. This is useful for holidays, business closures, or emergencies when your team isn’t available to answer queue calls. Here’s a breakdown of each queue destination you can choose from: AI Receptionist . Send callers to a RingCentral AIR extension. Announcement . Play an audio recording. Voicemail . Send missed calls to voicemail. External number . Forward the call to a number outside of RingCentral. A specific user . Send calls to a specific user. Multiple users – call queue . Send calls to a shared call queue where multiple team members can answer the phone. IVR menu . Send calls to a phone menu. Delegated line . Send calls to multiple people on a shared number. Shared line . Send calls to multiple devices on a shared number. Limited extension . Send calls to a phone in a common area, like an office desk phone. Site . Send calls to an extension at a different company site. For example, you could send a sales call from your Norfolk division to your Richmond site. How to set up additional RingCentral call routing features Need to set up a more complex call flow? You can combine call forwarding with RingCentral’s other call routing features. This includes multi-level IVR, call transfers, and ring groups. How to set up RingCentral IVR RingCentral’s IVR phone menus let callers route themselves to the right person or department. You may have also heard IVR called a virtual receptionist or auto-receptionist. Here’s how to set up RingCentral’s IVR feature: In the Admin Portal on the RingCentral desktop and web app, click Phone System . Under Company , click IVR Menus (b) , then New IVR Menu . Add keys under the Add Key dropdown box. Decide how these keypad dials should route callers. This could be: Routing the caller to a specific extension Transferring to a voicemail inbox Connecting to a dial-by-name directory Transferring to an external number Decide what happens if callers enter the wrong number or don’t press anything. Click Validate Menus to check for problems with your IVR menu. To finalize your menu, tap Save. Keep in mind there’s also a visual IVR menu builder and an XML Editor if you’d prefer to build your phone menus another way. How to transfer calls in RingCentral You can transfer live calls to any number or voicemail inbox directly from the RingCentral mobile app. Use the following steps to set this up: While on a live call, tap the three-dot More icon. Select Transfer . Choose your transfer type: Ask first. Give context to a team member before transferring a call over. Also known as a warm transfer. Transfer now. Transfer a call without speaking to the recipient first. Also known as a cold transfer. To voicemail. Send the caller to a specific person’s voicemail without ringing the number. Search for the person, extension, or external number you want to transfer to. For a warm transfer, wait until the recipient answers and brief them on the call before completing the transfer. Tap or click Complete Transfer to finish. How to set up ring order in RingCentral RingCentral also lets you control the order in which calls ring your devices and team members. Here are the options available to RingEX users: Ring in order. Ring numbers or devices one at a time in a sequence you set. If the first person doesn’t answer, the call moves to the next. Ring all together. Ring all numbers or devices at once until someone picks up the phone. For call queues, you have additional ring order options: Longest idle. Ring whichever team member has been inactive the longest. This can help distribute call volume evenly across your team. Fixed order. Rings team members one at a time in a specific sequence. This is useful when you want to prioritize certain reps before others. You can adjust ring order settings under Call handling & forwarding in your RingCentral phone settings. Or you can make changes at the queue level in the Admin Portal. RingCentral call forwarding limitations RingCentral seems to offer plenty of routing features at first glance. But once you start building a custom flow for your business, you’ll see its call forwarding limitations firsthand. Here are four reasons why RingCentral’s call forwarding settings fall short: 1. No visual call flow builder RingCentral doesn’t have a visual interface to set up and manage your call flows. It has one for IVRs, but not for your call flow. Without a visual interface, it can be hard to see your call flow paths as you set up different ring groups, multi-level IVRs, and working hour schedules. 2. Setup complexity Setting up your call management and routing settings in RingCentral can be tedious. Each setting needs to be toggled on and modified in the admin portal. As one RingCentral review states: “The platform is overly complicated and not intuitive, especially for small business owners who need something simple and reliable. Basic tasks take far more time than they should, and the overall setup process feels unnecessarily complex.” — Trustpilot 3. No backup call forwarding to AI Receptionist RingCentral’s AI Receptionist add-on can only take incoming calls as they come in. That means you can’t forward unanswered calls to it as a backup call routing option. You can forward calls from the receptionist to a rep, but not vice versa. You can’t put callers back into the AIR queue. This could create problems for businesses with high call volumes. If you route callers to voicemail, they’re more likely to hang up and try reaching out to your competition. 4. No call flow scheduling RingCentral doesn’t let you set up multiple call flows to schedule when needed. For example, you can’t schedule a special call flow for a holiday and let it automatically take over from your default call flow. You’ll have to manually set up your working hours each time, which can be tricky when you’re moving fast or are out of the office. You’ll also need to remember to adjust your settings again when you’re back to your regular working hours. How Quo offers more call routing flexibility RingCentral does offer call handling and forwarding features. They’re just not designed for teams with complex or fluctuating schedules. The good news is there’s a better alternative. Quo is a modern business phone system with more customizable call forwarding options than RingCentral. Each plan comes with unlimited calls and texts for Canadian and US numbers. You can also handle call forwarding as a team, with access to shared numbers, ring groups, and more. See how Quo matches up to RingCentral below. RingCentral call forwarding vs Quo at a glance Here’s how RingCentral’s call forwarding features compare to Quo’s: Feature Quo RingCentral Visual drag-and-drop call flow builder ✅, available on all plans ❌ Call forwarding to AI receptionist ✅ ❌ Multiple call flows ✅ ❌ Call flow scheduling ✅ ❌ Let’s explore these call forwarding features in greater detail. 1. Visual drag-and-drop call flow builder Each Quo plan comes with a visual call flow builder. It lets non-technical users set call forwarding settings by dragging and dropping blocks in a visual canvas. That way, you can build complex call flows with: Multi-level IVR phone menus Conditional ring groups Backup call options Business hours and after-hours routing Set up specific forwarding options in minutes to ensure no call goes unanswered. You can forward calls to external numbers after hours or create overflow paths during busy periods. You can even route calls to Sona, Quo’s AI agent, for 24/7 availability. Speaking of Sona… 2. Forward calls to AI voice agents Teams can forward incoming calls to Sona , Quo’s AI voice agent, to take calls when reps are busy or unavailable. Sona is built into Quo’s business phone platform so callers don’t have to leave voicemails or wait for callbacks. First, train Sona on your company information. This could be your website, knowledge pages, or vocabulary that callers are likely to use. Then provide custom scripts for specific scenarios. For example, you can instruct Sona to transfer urgent calls to your on-call staff after hours. All Sona calls will appear in your Quo workspace with a call transcript and summary as soon as they end. That way, you can get immediate context into past interactions and decide on next steps, if any, for the caller. Sona is also much more customizable than RingCentral. Unlike AIR, which requires a dedicated number or extension, Sona can handle calls in your primary business number. You can have Sona handle calls when your team is unavailable, or it can act as a backup routing option.You can also add Sona as a phone menu option, which is great for callers with quick questions and who don’t need an extensive conversation. Thousands of users say Sona is the easiest way to save time, build customer relationships, and never miss a call. No need to take our word for it, though: “Before using Sona, we were drowning in repetitive questions from clients and tenants. Missed calls left us feeling like we were always one step behind. But since bringing Sona onboard, all those repeat questions are handled automatically, and no call goes unanswered.” – Gabe Chase, Owner, Brentwood Property Group 3. Scheduled call flows Need to switch up your schedule for a time, then set it back to your regular hours? With Quo, teams can set up multiple call flows and add them to their schedule as needed. Let’s say you have a one-week vacation on the horizon. You can use temporary call flows to create alternate call routing setups, then switch between them without editing your default flow. This might be useful for: Holidays or seasonal campaigns. Run unique greetings or routing during special offers or events. Meetings or short unavailability. Route calls to Sona or another destination while you’re unavailable. Temporary staffing or routing changes. Route calls to another team member while you’re away.You can easily schedule when specific flows should start and end. Or you can manually select them yourself from your list of call flows. Learn more about why businesses switch from RingCentral to Quo Wondering how else Quo stacks up to RingCentral? Learn more in our Quo vs RingCentral comparison. FAQs Can RingCentral forward calls to an external number? Yes. RingCentral supports forwarding calls to external numbers, including mobile phones and landlines. To do this, go to your admin portal. Then go to the user’s forwarding rules and select External Number as the destination. What’s the difference between RingCentral call forwarding and call flip? Call forwarding routes incoming calls to another number. Call flip moves a call you’re already on from one device to another, like from your desk phone to your cell. You should use call forwarding for unanswered calls and call flip for live calls between devices. How do I forward calls only after business hours? To forward calls only after business hours with RingCentral, you’ll need to set up after-hours call forwarding. Here’s how: 1. In your RingCentral account, click your profile picture at the top left, then click Incoming call rules. 2. Toggle on Forward all calls . Then choose Forward the call under the dropdown box. You can send incoming calls to any forwarding number or extension within the RingCentral app. 3. Click Add schedule , then set your call forwarding schedule using the date and time selectors. This rule will forward all after-hours incoming calls to the number or extension of your choice. Why is my RingCentral call forwarding not working? The most common causes for RingCentral call forwarding to not work are: • A forwarding rule that wasn’t saved or enabled • An admin-level setting that’s overriding a user-level rule • The destination number not including the country code Don’t forget to check if external call forwarding is permitted on your plan.

title: GoTab POS Review: What Operators Should Know About the Tab-First System
summary: GoTab runs open tabs, not tickets. Real pricing from $15 to $229 a month, the 2.40% + 15 cent processing math, and which venues it fits. From an operator.
body_text: Key takeaways GoTab is built around the open tab. Guests scan, order, and keep a tab running from anywhere in the venue. That makes it a strong fit for breweries, taprooms, food halls and hotels, and an odd fit for fast counter lines. Software runs $15 to $229 a month depending on tier. The real bill is processing at 2.40% plus 15 cents per in-person transaction, with extra charges for Amex and international cards. The add-ons stack up. Extra stations and kitchen screens run $25 to $35 a month each, loyalty and gift cards $35, delivery aggregation $55. If you take reservations or host private events, your phone is its own revenue channel, and those calls arrive during the exact hours your team is buried. My family's restaurants ran from takeaway counters to a brewery, and I was helping manage 11 of them by age 17. The brewery taught me something the takeaways never did: some venues do not run on tickets. They run on tabs that stay open for three hours while a group drifts from the bar to the patio. GoTab is the first POS I have reviewed that was actually designed for that guest. At Certus we work with hundreds of restaurants across every major POS, so I see what operators actually live with after the sales demo. Here is my honest read on GoTab: where it earns its keep, what it really costs, and the channel it was never asked to carry. What GoTab is GoTab calls itself a commerce platform for hospitality, and the label fits better than "restaurant POS." The system is built for venues where guests move around and keep spending: breweries, taprooms, food halls, hotels, bars, and entertainment venues. Reviewers consistently describe it as strongest in exactly those rooms, with venues running 2,500 or more tabs in a single day on it. The core idea is the shared, portable tab. A guest scans a QR code, opens a tab, and orders from their phone. They can add rounds from the patio, split with friends, and close out without flagging anyone down. Your staff take orders on handhelds too, and both flows land on the same tab. For a brewery pouring for a Saturday crowd, that is the whole game: fewer lines at the bar, more rounds ordered, nobody waiting to pay. There is no per-cover fee. GoTab charges for software and processing, and does not take a cut per guest served, which matters at high-volume venues where per-cover models get expensive fast. GoTab pricing: the real math GoTab publishes three software tiers. As of July 2026: Basic: $15 a month. The entry point for simple setups. Pro: $99 a month. The tier most full venues actually need. Sync: $229 a month. Adds on-premises failover, so the system keeps working if your internet drops. Processing starts at 2.40% plus 15 cents per in-person transaction. Amex adds 0.85% on top. International cards add 1.5%. Run that against your own card mix before you decide anything, because a venue doing $80,000 a month in cards pays roughly $1,900 a month in processing at the base rate. The software fee is a rounding error next to that. Then come the add-ons. Extra POS stations, kitchen display screens, and kiosks run $25 to $35 a month each. Loyalty and gift cards cost $35 a month. Delivery aggregation, which pulls your delivery apps into one screen, is $55 a month. Setup fees are quoted per venue rather than published, and GoTab offers 0% financing over 24 to 36 months if you want to spread hardware costs. A realistic Pro setup for a mid-size taproom, with two extra stations, a kitchen screen, and loyalty, lands around $200 to $250 a month in software before processing. That is honest money, and still cheaper than most of the category if the tab model fits how you serve. What operators like The tab model is the review theme that repeats everywhere. Guests order more when ordering is easy, and nothing is easier than adding a round from your seat. Venues report the QR flow genuinely reduces bar lines instead of just moving them. The pricing structure earns praise too. Flat software tiers with no per-cover fees mean a packed Saturday does not raise your bill. And the Sync tier's offline failover answers the question every operator asks about cloud systems: what happens when the wifi dies mid-service. Where it struggles Point it at the wrong venue and the strengths invert. Reviewers describe GoTab as overbuilt for fast counter service. If your whole operation is a line of people ordering burritos to go, the tab machinery is weight you carry without using. A counter-service spot is usually better served by the mainstream systems, and I have written full operator reviews of Toast , Square , Clover , and SkyTab with real fees in each. The add-on stack deserves a hard look too. $15 a month is the advertised number, but almost nobody runs a real venue on Basic alone. Price the tier and add-ons you will actually use, the same discipline I push in every review here. And GoTab is a smaller company than the giants it competes with. That cuts both ways: operators report more direct attention than they got from the big platforms, and a smaller integration shelf than Toast or Square offers. The verdict If you run a brewery, taproom, food hall, hotel outlet, or any room where guests roam and tabs stay open, GoTab deserves a spot on your shortlist. It was built for your service model, the pricing respects your volume, and the $99 Pro tier is fair for what it does. If you run counter service or a straightforward takeaway, skip it. You would be paying for machinery designed around a guest who does not visit your restaurant. Start with the mainstream reviews linked above instead. Reservations, private events, and your phone If you are the type of venue that is looking at GoTab in the first place, chances are you take reservations, host private events, or both. That matters more than it sounds, because bookings are the one part of your operation that will never arrive through a QR code. They come from people who have not walked in yet, they almost always arrive by phone, and they land during service, when nobody can step away from the bar to answer. The money on those calls is real. A brewery's best Saturday is often the one a stranger tried to book three weeks earlier, whether that was a 40-person birthday, a company happy hour, or a rehearsal dinner, and DoorDash research reported by Restaurant Dive found that half of all calls to restaurants go unanswered. Losing a single event inquiry can outweigh a whole night of walk-in bar sales. Then there is the steady drip of questions: are dogs allowed on the patio, do you take walk-ins, is there parking, can we watch the game. Each one pulls a staff member off the floor for a couple of minutes, dozens of times a day, and not one of them actually needed a human. That workload is what we built Certus AI for. It answers every call around the clock in English or Spanish, both included, handles the routine questions straight from your own menu and policies, and takes reservations and books them through OpenTable. When a caller wants to talk about a 40-person event, it captures the details and routes the inquiry to your team instead of losing it to voicemail. For venues that take phone orders too, it sends those straight into the POS, and it works with all major POS systems including Toast, Square, Clover, Skytab, and Aloha NCR. It runs on flat monthly pricing with a 30-day rolling contract, setup happens the same day, and a 30-day money-back guarantee stands behind all of it. Our Trustpilot rating is 4.5 stars. Book a demo and ask it your venue's five most annoying questions, then ask it to book a table. About the author I'm Gurveer Singh, CEO and co-founder of Certus AI. We work with hundreds of restaurants across every major POS, from single-location independents to chains and franchises. Before this I managed 11 of my family's restaurants by age 17, from takeaways to breweries, which is where I learned that the till you pick matters less than the calls you never hear about. The project is expected to create 136 new jobs over […]
body_text: GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Aug. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — UFP Industries, Inc. (Nasdaq: UFPI ) today announced plans to establish a new UFP Packaging manufacturing facility in Cherokee County, South Carolina, expanding its Structural Packaging capacity and strengthening its ability to serve national industrial customers with custom, value-added packaging solutions. The project is expected to create 136 new jobs over five years and represents an investment of approximately $5.31 million in real property, machinery and equipment. The facility will manufacture wood packaging products and strengthen UFP Packaging’s ability to serve industrial customers, especially those with highly-technical needs, across the Southeast and beyond. “This project is a strong example of how we are investing in our higher-margin core businesses while expanding the capabilities that differentiate UFP in the market,” said Will Schwartz , President and CEO of UFP Industries. “We’ve discussed the significant progress our Structural Packaging business unit is making with strategic customers across the industrial economy. This investment supports that strategy. It gives us added capacity, expands our geographic reach and enhances our ability to deliver highly customized solutions that help customers solve difficult packaging and logistics challenges. It also gives us the opportunity to build a team the UFP way — by developing people, promoting from within and creating careers that last. South Carolina’s strong manufacturing base, skilled workforce and values-driven business environment make it the right fit for our company and our culture.” UFP Packaging serves industrial, manufacturing and logistics customers with a broad portfolio of packaging products and services, including structural packaging, pallet solutions and protective packaging. Its Structural Packaging business designs and manufactures custom wood, steel, foam and mixed-material packaging solutions for customers with demanding shipping, storage and product-protection requirements. “Structural Packaging is one of the clearest examples of where our scale, technical knowledge and customer relationships come together,” said Scott Worthington , President of UFP Packaging. “Our teams are not simply selling boxes or crates. They are working with customers to understand what they make, how it moves, what risks it faces in transit and how we can design a better solution. This facility and the local South Carolinians who run it will help us support large, national customers with the consistency, engineering support and responsiveness they need as their own operations grow.” The planned South Carolina facility will position UFP Packaging closer to important industrial customers and transportation corridors while increasing production flexibility across its national manufacturing network. It also reflects UFP Industries’ continued focus on value-added products, operational excellence and disciplined capital deployment. “This is exactly the type of opportunity we are focused on,” Schwartz continued. “It strengthens a core business, supports above-market growth and reinforces our long-term goal of improving margins and returns by providing more value to our customers, who are often among the nation’s top innovators. We are grateful for the support of Cherokee County and the State of South Carolina, and we look forward to building a strong team and operation in the region.” The project remains subject to customary approvals and finalization of related agreements. About UFP Industries, Inc. UFP Industries, Inc. is a holding company whose operating subsidiaries, UFP Packaging, UFP Construction and UFP Retail Solutions, manufacture, distribute and sell a wide variety of value-added products used in residential and commercial construction, packaging and other industrial applications worldwide. Founded in 1955, the company is headquartered in Grand Rapids, Michigan, with affiliates in North America, Europe, Asia and Australia. For more about UFP Industries, visit www.ufpi.com . With strong year-to-date results and closing of the Cornerstone Acquisition, we are raising our 2026 guidance as well as increasing the 2027 and 2028 outlooks,” said Talen Chief Executive Officer Mac McFarland. During the second quarter 2026, we repurchased 550,000 shares of TEC common stock for approximately $200 million. All share repurchase amounts exclude transaction costs. Financing Transactions In April 2026, Talen subsidiary, Talen Energy Supply, LLC (“TES”) issued in private placement transactions not involving a public offering: (i) $1.5 billion in aggregate principal amount of 6.125% senior unsecured notes due 2031; and (ii) $2.5 billion in aggregate principal amount of 6.375% senior unsecured notes due 2033. The net proceeds from the issuance and sale of the unsecured notes due 2031 and 2033 were used to (i) fund the Cornerstone Acquisition; and (ii) redeem in full $1.2 billion of outstanding 8.625% senior secured notes due 2030. As of July 31, 2026, Talen had ample total available liquidity of approximately $1.9 billion, comprised of $525 million of unrestricted cash and $1.4 billion of available capacity under the RCF. Non-GAAP financial measures do not have definitions under GAAP and may be defined and calculated differently by, and not be comparable to, similarly titled measures used by other companies. Non-GAAP measures are not intended to replace the most comparable GAAP measures as indicators of performance. Generally, a non-GAAP financial measure is a numerical measure of financial performance, financial position, or cash flows that excludes (or includes) amounts that are included in (or excluded from) the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. Management cautions readers not to place undue reliance on the following non-GAAP financial measures, but to also consider them along with their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP measures have limitations as analytical tools and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for analyzing our results as reported under GAAP. Adjusted EBITDA We use Adjusted EBITDA to: (i) assist in comparing operating performance and readily view operating trends on a consistent basis from period to period without certain items that may distort financial results; (ii) plan and forecast overall expectations and evaluate actual results against such expectations; (iii) communicate with our Board of Directors, shareholders, creditors, analysts, and the broader financial community concerning our financial performance; (iv) set performance metrics for our annual short-term incentive compensation; and (v) assess compliance with our indebtedness. Adjusted EBITDA is computed as net income (loss) adjusted, among other things, for certain: (i) nonrecurring charges; (ii) non-recurring gains; (iii) non-cash and other items; (iv) unusual market events; (v) any depreciation, amortization, or accretion; (vi) mark-to-market gains or losses; (vii) gains and losses on the nuclear facility decommissioning trust (“NDT”); (viii) gains and losses on asset sales, dispositions, and asset retirement; (ix) impairments, obsolescence, and net realizable value charges; (x) interest expense; (xi) income taxes; (xii) legal settlements, liquidated damages, and contractual terminations; (xiii) development expenses; (xiv) noncontrolling interests, except where otherwise noted; and (xv) other adjustments. Such adjustments are computed consistently with the provisions of our indebtedness to the extent that they can be derived from the financial records of the business. Additionally, we believe investors commonly adjust net income (loss) information to eliminate the effect of nonrecurring restructuring expenses and other non-cash charges, which can vary widely from company to company and from period to period and impair comparability. We believe Adjusted EBITDA is useful to investors and other users of our financial statements to evaluate our operating performance because it provides an additional tool to compare business performance across companies and between periods. Adjusted EBITDA is widely used by investors to measure a company’s operating performance without regard to such items described above. These adjustments can vary substantially from company to company and period to period depending upon accounting policies, book value of assets, capital structure, and the method by which assets were acquired. Adjusted Free Cash Flow Adjusted Free Cash Flow is utilized by our chief operating decision makers to evaluate cash flow activities. Adjusted Free Cash Flow is computed as Adjusted EBITDA reduced by capital expenditures (including nuclear fuel but excluding development, growth, and (or) conversion capital expenditures), cash payments for interest and finance charges, cash payments for income taxes (excluding income taxes paid from the NDT, taxes paid or deductions taken as a result of strategic asset sales, and benefits of the Nuclear PTC utilized to reduce income taxes paid), and pension contributions. We believe Adjusted Free Cash Flow is useful to investors and other users of our financial statements in evaluating our operating performance because it provides them with an additional tool to determine a company’s ability to meet future obligations and to compare business performance across companies and across periods. Adjusted Free Cash Flow is widely used by investors to measure a company’s levered cash flow without regard to items such as ARO settlements; nonrecurring development, growth and conversion expenditures; and cash proceeds or payments for the sale or purchase of assets, which can vary substantially from company to company and from period to period depending upon accounting methods, book value of assets, capital structure, and the method by which assets were acquired. title: The Cheapest New Trucks on Sale in 2026
summary: Is there such a thing as a cheap new truck any more? Absolutely! Here's our expert guide to the top 10 cheapest new trucks on sale.
body_text: If you're shopping for a new truck in 2026 and want to keep your budget in check, you're facing a market where "affordable" means something different than it did a few years ago. Entry-level pricing has climbed across the board, but there are still pickups that deliver real capability without forcing you into luxury-truck territory. The cheapest new trucks available this year range from compact unibody models that prioritize fuel economy and daily drivability to traditional body-on-frame midsize and full-size pickups built for towing, hauling, and weekend work. Understanding where each truck fits—and what tradeoffs come with a lower sticker price—can help you find the right balance between upfront cost and long-term value. This guide covers 10 trucks that offer relatively attainable entry points in 2026, spanning compact models like the Ford Maverick and Hyundai Santa Cruz, midsize options including the Toyota Tacoma and Chevrolet Colorado, and full-size pickups like the GMC Sierra 1500 and Chevrolet Silverado 1500. Some deliver standout fuel economy or standard hybrid powertrains, while others focus on maximum configurability or proven off-road capability. We'll walk through what each truck offers for the money, where it excels, and what compromises you'll need to accept if you're chasing the lowest possible price. Toyota Tacoma CarGurus expert rating: 7.8 out of 10 CarGurus user rating: 4.5 out of 5 Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus: 32.3% Overall CarGurus rating: 4.6 out of 5 Pros Cons Excellent reputation for reliability Noisy cabin Great off-road capability Manual-adjust seats can be troublesome Standard advanced driver-assistance tech Interior skews functional even in the top trim For shoppers cross-shopping the cheapest new trucks available in 2026, the Tacoma's fourth-generation redesign matters because it brings more power and more standard equipment without wandering too far from the simple, tough formula Tacoma buyers expect. Most trims use a 2.4-liter turbocharged four-cylinder making 278 hp and 317 lb-ft of torque (the base SR is tuned to 228 hp and 243 lb-ft), and Toyota pairs it with an eight-speed automatic or an available six-speed manual. Fuel economy is part of the value story, too: Toyota estimates even the least efficient manual four-wheel drive (4WD) version at 20 miles per gallon (MPG) combined, with automatic 4WD up to 21 MPG combined and 2WD versions estimated as high as 23 MPG combined. Usability got a real upgrade, especially if you've lived with older Tacoma packaging. The old small rear-seat layout is gone, replaced by a two-door XtraCab that treats the space behind the seats as lockable cargo storage, while Double Cab models keep family-duty in play and add more under-seat storage than before. Tech now fits the modern market with an 8-inch touchscreen standard (and an available 14-inch screen), plus wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and there's meaningful towing help available like a trailer brake controller and an accessory wireless trailer camera. Safety equipment is also stronger for the money, with Toyota Safety Sense 3.0 standard, including lane-centering (Lane Tracing Assist), plus available blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert on most trims. The CarGurus Verdict: "The fourth-gen Tacoma is also the first Tacoma to share a platform with the larger Toyota Tundra. (The TNGA-F platform also underpins the Sequoia and the just-revived Land Cruiser.) It launches in six trim levels, each powered by a turbocharged four-cylinder engine, and the Tacoma's first-ever hybrid powertrain is due in the spring of 2024, along with two additional trims. The lineup's standard hybrid setup makes a big difference at the pump: the front-wheel drive (FWD) hybrid is EPA-rated at 38 MPG combined, and the new-for-2025 all-wheel drive (AWD) hybrid is right behind at 37 MPG combined. Just keep expectations in check on bargain-basement pricing—Ford's own note is that "the Maverick lineup grows as prices rise," and the 2025 Maverick starts at $29,840 including destination. Even at its compact size, the Maverick is built to do truck jobs: every model tows 2,000 pounds, and most trims (excluding Tremor and Lobo) can be upgraded to 4,000 pounds with the 4K Towing Package; the bed measures 4.5 feet, and the tailgate can be positioned to help carry longer items like 4x8 sheets. For 2025, tech takes a step forward with Sync 4, a standard 13.2-inch touchscreen, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, and an 8-inch digital gauge cluster, though some climate functions still live in the screen. The most affordable new trucks in 2026 generally start in the high-$20,000 to low-$30,000 range, depending on the model and configuration. Compact and sport-truck options tend to carry the lowest base prices, while midsize and full-size trucks typically start higher. Keep in mind that destination charges, required packages, and popular options can push the final price well above the advertised starting MSRP, so it's worth checking current listings in your area for real transaction prices. What's the difference between a compact truck, a midsize truck, and a full-size truck? Compact trucks (sometimes called "sport trucks") are the smallest and most car-like in the segment, prioritizing fuel efficiency and everyday drivability over heavy-duty capability. Midsize trucks offer a balance of capability and manageability, with more towing and payload capacity than compact options while still fitting in a standard garage. Full-size trucks are the largest and most capable, with the highest tow ratings and payload numbers, but they also carry the highest base prices and operating costs. Your best choice depends on how you plan to use the truck day-to-day. Are cheap new trucks good on gas? Fuel economy varies widely across the segment. Hybrid-powered compact trucks can achieve impressive efficiency — some exceeding 35 mpg combined — while midsize and full-size trucks with turbocharged four-cylinder or V6 engines typically return 18–23 mpg combined in real-world driving. Diesel engine options on full-size trucks can improve highway efficiency significantly. If fuel costs are a priority, it's worth comparing EPA estimates alongside real-world owner-reported figures before making a decision. What should I look for when buying a cheap new truck? Beyond the sticker price, focus on total cost of ownership: fuel economy, standard safety features (some budget trims omit blind-spot monitoring and other key driver-assistance tech), warranty coverage, and projected reliability. Also consider how you'll actually use the truck — towing capacity, payload rating, bed length, and cab size all affect whether a given model fits your needs. CarGurus Deal Ratings and Instant Market Value (IMV) pricing can help you determine whether a specific listing is priced fairly relative to the market. Do cheap new trucks come with modern safety features? It depends on the model and trim level. Some manufacturers include a robust suite of driver-assistance technology as standard equipment even on base trims, while others reserve features like blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, and rear cross-traffic alert for higher trim levels. Before purchasing, review the standard safety equipment on the specific trim you're considering, and check available crash-test ratings from NHTSA and IIHS to get a complete picture of real-world safety performance. What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different? Most car-shopping websites publish lists of the best cars across a variety of categories, with recommendations generally driven by editorial expertise. Here's what makes ours different: In addition to the insights and verdicts of our team of car-testing experts, our best cars guides take into account other factors that we know matter to buyers-real owner experiences and current market value. Our expert reviewers are among this country's most trusted automotive journalists, also writing for publications including US News and World Report, Edmunds, Digital Trends, J.D. Power, and Car & Driver. They put each car through real-world testing and create detailed reviews of performance in a range of categories, from practicality and driving manners to cost-effectiveness and safety. We also analyze hundreds of thousands of used car listings on CarGurus.com to track which models consistently offer the highest percentage of best deals relative to how many are listed for sale. Then we factor in reviews from owners-people who actually live with these cars every day. Our proprietary Best Cars algorithm then creates a final Overall CarGurus rating combining expert scores, user reviews, and the percentage of listings that have earned the Good or Great Deal rating. This multi-pronged approach reveals not just which cars excel on paper, but which ones deliver satisfaction and value when you're ready to buy. title: Cloudastructure Wins Full Guard Replacement Across Five-Building Southern California Office Portfolio for One of the World's Largest Commercial Real Estate Firms
summary: Recommended Reading
body_text: Expansion Follows Direct Referral From Sister Property Within the Same Institutional Tenant Portfolio Highlights Growing Adoption of AI-Powered Remote Guarding Across Commercial Real Estate PALO ALTO, Calif., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cloudastructure, Inc. ("Cloudastructure" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: CSAI) , an award-winning provider of AI-powered surveillance, remote monitoring, and cloud-based security analytics, today announced it will deploy its AI Surveillance and Remote Guarding platform across a five-building commercial office portfolio in Southern California, fully replacing the property's dedicated onsite security guard with camera-based monitoring and live remote guarding. The transition is scheduled to begin in late summer 2026, with full operations targeted for mid-September. The deployment expands Cloudastructure's relationship with one of the world's largest commercial real estate services and investment firms, which manages the portfolio on behalf of its ownership. The opportunity resulted from a direct referral by a sister property within the same institutional tenant's portfolio, reinforcing the Company's land-and-expand strategy. None of the portfolio's five buildings currently has camera coverage at its lobby entrances, so Cloudastructure will design and install the surveillance infrastructure across the entire property from the ground up. Greenfield deployments like this represent some of the Company's most attractive opportunities, allowing it to capture the full installation footprint while establishing a larger recurring subscription base. "Replacing a round-the-clock guard post with our platform isn't just a cost decision for property owners, it's a reliability decision," said Ed Burnett, Chief of Operations and Security at Cloudastructure. "Onsite guards get sick, take breaks, and turn over; a guard shortage or a staffing gap can leave a lobby uncovered with no notice. Our AI-powered analytics and live remote guarding never clock out. They flag activity in real time, and a remote guard can respond immediately, every hour of every day. For a portfolio like this one, that's a more consistent security model than relying on a single onsite officer, often at a lower total cost." Rising guard wages, persistent staffing shortages and growing demand for around-the-clock coverage are driving more commercial landlords to evaluate AI-powered remote guarding as an alternative to traditional onsite personnel. This deployment represents Cloudastructure's first commercial office portfolio to fully replace an onsite guard program with remote guarding at scale and further expands the Company's presence beyond its core multifamily business. As adoption continues across commercial real estate, Cloudastructure believes its platform is well positioned to support this transition. About Cloudastructure Headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Cloudastructure's patented, advanced, award-winning security platform utilizes a scalable cloud-based architecture that features cloud video surveillance with proprietary, state-of-the-art AI/ML analytics, and a seamless remote guarding solution. The combination enables enterprise businesses to achieve proactive, end-to-end security, and pairs that platform with an attractive value proposition that eschews proprietary hardware and offers contract-free, month-to-month pricing and unlimited 24/7 support. With Cloudastructure, companies can achieve unparalleled situational awareness in real time and thereby stop crime as it is happening, while simultaneously achieving up to a 75% lower Total Cost of Ownership than other systems. For more information, visit https://www.cloudastructure.com/. body_text: Investor Contact For investor related questions, please email investors@aclaristx.com Press Release View all press releases » PDF Version Aclaris Therapeutics Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate and Clinical Update August 6, 2026 - Full Top Line Results from Phase 1a SAD/MAD Trial of ATI-052 Validate Potential Best-in-Class Potency Advantage and Opportunity for Extended Dosing - - Timelines Reaffirmed for Upcoming Top Line Results from Phase 1b Proof-of-Concept (POC) Trials of ATI-052 and Phase 2 Trial of Bosakitug (ATI-045) - - Strong Cash Runway Expected to Enable Development of Pipeline Through the End of 2028 - WAYNE, Pa., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: ACRS), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel product candidates for immuno-inflammatory diseases, today announced its financial results for the second quarter of 2026 and provided a corporate and clinical update. “The first half of 2026 was a period of strong execution across the organization, positioning Aclaris for an exciting second half of the year with numerous expected key catalysts,” stated Dr. Neal Walker, Chief Executive Officer and Chair of the Board of Directors of Aclaris. “We expect to provide three clinical data readouts, including placebo-controlled top line results from our two Phase 1b POC trials of our anti-TSLP/IL-4Rα bispecific antibody ATI-052 in both asthma and atopic dermatitis and the Phase 2 AD trial of our anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody bosakitug. Other key catalysts include initiation of a Phase 2b clinical program with ATI-052 and a Phase 2b trial in lichen planus with modzatinib. Finally, our data presented recently at the FASEB Immunoreceptors and Immunotherapy conference support the best-in-class potential of our investigational ITK inhibitor ATI-9494, for which we expect to file an IND late this year.” Second Quarter 2026 Highlights, Recent Updates and Upcoming Catalysts Pipeline: Biologics: Antibody Franchise Provided Positive Full Top Line Results of Phase 1a Single (SAD) and Multiple Ascending Dose (MAD) Trial of Investigational Bispecific Anti-TSLP/IL-4R α Antibody ATI-052 Validating Potency and Potential for Extended Dosing: ATI-052 was well tolerated and demonstrated a favorable safety profile. The combination of the strong and sustained PK duration and PD effect supported the potential for up to quarterly dosing. (press release here ) Reaffirmed Expectation of Top Line Results in the Second Half of 2026 from Two Ongoing Phase 1b POC Trials of ATI- 052: ATI-052 is being assessed in POC trials in both atopic dermatitis (AD) and asthma. Confirmed Intent to Initiate a Phase 2b Program Encompassing Asthma and AD with ATI-052 in the Fourth Quarter of 2026: Aclaris expects the clinical program to commence with a Phase 2b trial in asthma in the fourth quarter of 2026. The Company also now expects to commence startup activities for a Phase 2b trial in AD and for a proof-of-concept (POC) trial in eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE). On Track for Expected Fourth Quarter 2026 Readout of Top Line Results from Phase 2 Trial of Investigational Anti-TSLP Monoclonal Antibody Bosakitug: Enrollment is complete in this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial designed to evaluate bosakitug in 109 patients with AD. (press release here ) Kinase Inhibitors: ITK Franchise Initiation of Phase 2b Clinical Program for Modzatinib (ATI-2138), a Potent and Selective Investigational Inhibitor of ITK and JAK3, Planned for the Fourth Quarter of 2026: Aclaris intends to initiate a multi-part Phase 2b trial of modzatinib in lichen planus, an unaddressed chronic, inflammatory, CD8-driven interface dermatitis. There are currently no approved therapies in this indication. (press release here ) On Track for Expected Fourth Quarter 2026 Filing of Investigational New Drug (IND) Application for ATI-9494, Aclaris’ Investigational Dual Inhibitor of ITK and TXK: ATI-9494 has demonstrated potent blockade of Th1 and Th2 responses, a prolonged half-life, and high potency against ITK, potentially enabling low drug burden, dosing flexibility, and once daily (QD) administration across a broad range of disease indications. Presented Data Characterizing Potency, Selectivity, and Target Occupancy of ATI-9494: New preclinical data presented at the 2026 Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology (FASEB) Immunoreceptors and Immunology Science Research Conference included results from cellular target engagement studies that demonstrated potent engagement of ITK by ATI-9494 and its ability to block functional activation of the TCR pathway. ATI-9494 demonstrated potency up to 25 times greater than soquelitinib (CPI-818) across multiple biochemical and functional cellular assays. Financial Results Liquidity and Capital Resources As of June 30, 2026, Aclaris had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $170.6 million compared to $151.4 million as of December 31, 2025. Subsequent to June 30, 2026, the Company sold 7.3 million shares of its common stock for aggregate gross proceeds of $40.2 million, pursuant to the Company’s at-the-market (ATM) agreement with Leerink Partners LLC and Cantor Fitzgerald & Co. Proceeds from these sales provide the Company with additional funds to support the planned commencement of startup activities for the Phase 2b trial of ATI-052 in AD and a POC trial in EoE. The Company believes that its cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities will be sufficient to fund its operations through the end of 2028, without giving effect to any potential business development transactions or additional financing activities. Second Quarter 2026 and Year-to-Date 2026 Net loss was $21.5 million for the second quarter of 2026 compared to $15.4 million for the second quarter of 2025. Net loss was $41.3 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to $30.5 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Total revenue was $1.6 million for the second quarter of 2026 compared to $1.8 million for the second quarter of 2025. Total revenue was $3.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to $3.2 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase for the six-month period was primarily driven by higher royalties earned under the Lilly and Sun Pharma license agreements. Research and development (R&D) expenses were $18.1 million and $33.7 million for the quarter and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $11.4 million and $23.0 million for the corresponding prior year periods. The increases were primarily driven by expenses related to ATI-052, including product candidate manufacturing costs and clinical development expenses associated with a Phase 1a program and Phase 1b programs in AD and asthma, as well as product candidate manufacturing costs for ATI-9494. General and administrative (G&A) expenses were $6.0 million and $12.8 million for the quarter and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $5.4 million and $11.5 million for the prior year periods. The increases were primarily due to an increase in professional and legal expenses as well as personnel expenses. Revaluation of contingent consideration resulted in a $0.3 million charge for each of the quarter and six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to charges of $1.5 million and $1.8 million for the prior year periods. The decreases were primarily due to changes to the probability of success for certain product candidates and lower discount rates being applied to potential payments during the quarter and six months ended June 30, 2025. About Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a pipeline of novel product candidates to address the needs of patients with immuno-inflammatory diseases who lack satisfactory treatment options. The Company has a multi-stage portfolio of product candidates powered by a robust R&D engine. For additional information, please visit www.aclaristx.com and follow Aclaris on LinkedIn . title: A Guide to Roofr's Instant Estimator Tool | Roofr
summary: Need roofing estimate software that really works? Want to give homeowners online quotes and capture leads? Get the lowdown on Roofr's Instant Estimator tool.
body_text: TL;DR Offering instant ballpark quotes gives homeowners immediate value, gets you a foot in the door, builds trust with your brand, and weeds out the tire kickers. Roofr's Instant Estimator tool lets you offer estimates not just from your website, but from anywhere. Read on to learn more. Not all leads are created equal. When you rely on a generic form on your website to capture interest, it's hard to know which ones need attention first. Knowing more about every lead from the jump lets you focus on the high-intent homeowners who are ready to close (and avoid the tire kickers). Without that visibility, sorting through leads becomes a brutal cycle of wasted time and wasted marketing effort. That’s where Roofr's Instant Estimator helps. What Is the Instant Estimator? Roofr's Instant Estimator is an online roofing estimate tool that lets homeowners get a custom quote for their roof within minutes. From your website, sure, but also right from your social profiles, flyers, through local realtors, or from ANY piece of marketing you put out. It’s a powerful lead qualification tool on its own. But the real magic happens when you connect it to your Roofr CRM to optimize your sales flow. Use Roofr measurements and proposals to optimize your sales process so you not only quote faster, but close faster. At its core, Instant Estimator automated quoting helps with: Speed to lead (every quote requested is yours to lose) Saving time (a LOT of time) on lead qualification The homeowner experience (helping you stand out from the other guys) Marketing optimization (to get the most out of every dollar spent) Let’s look at these a little closer. Qualify Leads with Instant Estimates Following up with every lead is slow. In the time it takes to get in touch with a qualified lead, it may be too late. Or maybe you get to leads fast only to have to haggle over pricing. Lead qualification is a two-way street. Homeowners need to trust you, but you also need to focus on the right leads for your business. The Instant Estimator does the heavy lifting for you. Collect important project details immediately Homeowners enter their address, timeline, job urgency, and other info when they request a quote. Now you know what you're working with. No back-and-forth needed. You can skip right to closing the job. Give homeowners confidence The Instant Estimator calculates the homeowner's roof and creates a quote based on the materials and prices you’ve set. Homeowners INSTANTLY get a quote they know is specific to them, displayed in ranges with options, so they have a rough idea of pricing. It sets realistic expectations, conditions leads without locking you into a promised price, and sets the stage for a good conversation when you call. No surprises. Stop wasting time on early quotes that go nowhere With roofing instant estimates handled automatically, you're not burning time on quotes for folks that aren't serious. Homeowners see a real number tied to their actual roof. That builds more trust than any figure you could quote cold over the phone. IE puts you and your leads on the same page That's a step ahead and a huuuuuge competitive advantage. Make your marketing go further Spending money on door hangers and digital ads? Are you relying on homeowners remembering your URL or phone number... or giving them immediate value in the form of a free instant roofing quote? Plenty of folks spend money on marketing without a way to easily capture the audience seeing your stuff. That's a great way to miss out on leads. Relying on generic forms is inefficient and causes dropoff, especially if leads can only find them on your website. The Instant Estimator delivers instant and accurate roof estimates, wherever your leads are coming from. Quicker speed-to-lead The Instant Estimator doesn’t generate more marketing leads. It won’t attract new leads on its own, or do your SEO for you, or make more people see your ads. What it will do is make that marketing much more efficient. Time to value is the key to marketing. The Instant Estimator makes it easy for homeowners to get what they really want: a price for their roof. The interactive digital experience also builds trust without the face-to-face conversation. Homeowners add their own details in real time so they know what they’re getting is accurate. Expand your lead capture — and get creative Add an Instant Estimator link or QR code to all your marketing material. Anything! Door hangers, business cards, digital ads, flyers, truck wraps, event banners. Homeowners can get an instant roofing quote from anywhere they see you. And anytime your leads get quotes, you get their details. Trackable urls for better reporting Not measuring your marketing means you have no clue what’s actually working! You want to put your money behind things that are actually bringing you leads. You can see lead performance for each Instant Estimator link you create , meaning you can analyze who, what, and where you’re getting the most leads. That means you can stop guessing what's working and put your budget behind what actually converts. Here's how to turn your IE links into QR codes, if you haven't tried that yet. Give homeowners what they want When it comes down to it, the homeowner experience is what wins jobs. You’re around 7x more likely to close a deal when you reach out within the first hour of a lead coming in. The Instant Estimator helps you get in touch with quality leads faster, AND delivers a convenient online experience to help you stand out from the competition. Homeowners want to research and compare options on their own so they feel in control of their own destiny. With the online estimator, they can get a customized quote before even speaking to your team. It's a win-win. The questionnaire builds trust Homeowners use their address to start the online quote, building trust that the quote they’re getting is customized to them. They’re informed and empowered when it comes time to make a decision. Stand out from the competition Homeowners get professional, branded quotes that are customized to their project needs. Delivering detailed quotes into the palm of their hand gets you two steps ahead of your competition and helps you stand out from a sea of generic forms and slow follow-ups. What's new with Instant Estimator Roofr's been rolling out IE updates based on real contractor feedback. Here's what's new: Google Reviews integration: Connect your Google Reviews right to your Instant Estimator and choose which reviews appear. Homeowner preview mode: Before you publish your estimator, preview exactly what homeowners will see. Make it perfect before going live. Draft and publish: Save an Instant Estimator as a draft and publish it when ready. Great if you're building out pricing or getting your materials set up. Marketing Templates: Access a library of pre-formatted Canva templates, marketing materials, and resources to help you promote your business. → Looking to take your IE to that next level? Take a look at these quick ways to get the most from your Instant Estimator setup . The Instant Estimator: Helping you work smarter When it comes to running a roofing business, contractors wear a lot of hats. Instant Estimator takes the guesswork out of lead qualification and improves efficiency across your marketing and sales pipeline, giving you back time to focus on all the other stuff. Explore the Instant Estimator for yourself. ‍ Frequently Asked Questions How accurate are Roofr's online estimates? Roofr's Instant Estimator tech is powered by the same satellite imagery that puts our measurement reports among the best in the industry. ‍ ‍ Quotes are displayed as price ranges based on the materials and pricing you've set in your account, so the numbers reflect your actual business. They're accurate enough to have a real pricing conversation while giving you room to finalize the quote after an inspection. Do online estimates replace in-person quotes? ‍ No, and in most cases they're not meant to. The Instant Estimator is a lead qualification and engagement tool to get homeowners invested and informed. You can still do an inspection and confirm scope later. Does an instant estimator help me get more leads? ‍ It doesn't replace your marketing. No magic shortcuts exist: you still need to drive traffic through ads, referrals, yard signs, or whatever's working for you. What the Instant Estimator does is convert more of that traffic into actual leads. Instead of a homeowner bouncing, they get a real quote. They get value, they appreciate and trust your brand, you win the job. Can I use the Instant Estimator outside of my website? ‍ Heck yeah you can. Each Instant Estimator has a unique link you can share anywhere: social media, your Google Business Profile , email campaigns, text messages, and so on. You can also generate a QR code from your link and add it to physical marketing materials. What happens to leads after they submit a quote? ‍ Lead details flow directly into your Roofr CRM, where you can see their contact info and the estimate they got. From there, you can follow up, assign the lead to a rep, and track them through your sales pipeline. If you're using Roofr's full platform, you can also move from lead to measurement to proposal without ever leaving the system. Start using Roofr for free or book a call with the team to see how it all fits together.

title: CF Industries Holdings, Inc. Reports First Half 2026 Net Earnings of $1.34 Billion, Adjusted EBITDA of $2.18 Billion
body_text: CF Industries Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: CF), a leading global manufacturer of hydrogen and nitrogen products, today announced results for the first half and second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Highlights First half 2026 net earnings(1) of $1.34 billion, or $8.71 per diluted share, EBITDA(2) of $2.17 billion, and adjusted EBITDA(2) of $2.18 billion. First half 2026 financial results include a gain of approximately $170 million from a litigation settlement Second quarter 2026 net earnings of $727 million, or $4.73 per diluted share, EBITDA of $1.17 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $1.19 billion Trailing twelve months net cash from operating activities of $2.98 billion; free cash flow(3) of $1.82 billion for same period, which includes cash inflows and outflows associated with the Blue Point One joint venture Repurchased 0 million shares for $230 million during the second quarter of 2026 Declared quarterly dividend of $0.60 per share of common stock in July 2026, a 20% increase over prior quarterly dividend In July 2026, received permits necessary to commence construction at Blue Point Complex in August “The CF Industries team operated safely and delivered excellent operational results despite rapidly changing customer dynamics,” said Chris Bohn, president and chief executive officer, CF Industries Holdings, Inc. “We believe the Company is positioned extremely well in the near- and longer-term, with our premium-grade North American asset base, disciplined strategic growth opportunities, including Blue Point, and strong balance sheet. As a result, we believe CF Industries will continue to generate substantial free cash flow, enabling us to build on our strong track record of investing in high-return initiatives and returning capital to shareholders through share repurchases and our increased quarterly dividend.” Read the complete press release .
